title: They welcomed Jesus with praise…
paragraphs: They welcomed Jesus with praise…
…and then demanded His crucifixion.

That shift did not happen overnight.
It only looked sudden.

Because the truth is—
the seeds of rejection were already hidden inside their praise.
Jerusalem knew how to celebrate Him.

They laid down garments.
They waved palm branches.
They shouted, “Hosanna to the Son of David!” (Matthew 21:9)

It was loud.
It was emotional.
It looked like revival.
But heaven sees deeper than volume.
Because a few days later, another sound rose from the same city:
“Crucify Him.” (Luke 23:21)
And that is one of the most uncomfortable warnings in all of Scripture:
You can praise Jesus… and still resist Him.
Pause there.

Because this is not just about them.
This is about us.
The crowd welcomed Jesus as long as He matched their expectations.

They thought He came to overthrow Rome.
They expected political power, immediate victory, visible dominance.
But Jesus came for something deeper.

He came to confront sin.
He came to call for repentance.
He came to establish a Kingdom not built on force—but surrender.
And when He didn’t become the King they imagined…
their praise collapsed.

“Their problem was not that they rejected Jesus later.
It was that they misunderstood Him from the beginning.”
That’s the warning.
Because many people still do this today.
We celebrate the parts of Jesus that feel good.

The Provider.
The Healer.
The Miracle Worker.
The One who opens doors.
But what happens when Jesus becomes the One who corrects you?

What happens when His Word confronts your lifestyle?
Your habits?
Your hidden compromises?
What happens when following Him costs you something?

Because the same crowd that shouted “Hosanna”
could not handle a Messiah who didn’t serve their agenda.
And here’s the uncomfortable truth:
A faith built on expectations will turn on God when He doesn’t follow your script.
Let that sink in.
Because many people don’t walk away from God due to lack of evidence…
They walk away because God didn’t meet their expectations.

He didn’t answer fast enough.
Didn’t move the way they wanted.
Didn’t protect their plans.
So slowly…

admiration turns into frustration.
And frustration—if left unchecked—turns into resistance.

“The same voice that praises God in comfort
can question Him in discomfort.”
The crowd didn’t suddenly become sinful on Friday.
Their hearts were already divided on Sunday.

They wanted a King without surrender.
A Savior without Lordship.
A crown without a cross.
And that is still one of the greatest dangers in modern faith.

Because it is possible to follow Jesus publicly…
but resist Him privately.

To sing about surrender…
but negotiate obedience.

To lift your hands in worship…
but hold back areas of your life He’s asking for.

“Not every ‘Hosanna’ comes from a surrendered heart.”
“Emotion can be real… and still be shallow.”
“Crowds can be loud… and still be lost.”
This is why Jesus never trusted crowds.

John 2:24 says He did not entrust Himself to them,
because He knew what was in man.
He could see the difference between excitement and commitment.
Between admiration and allegiance.

Between people who love what He does…
and people who submit to who He is.
So the real question is not:
“Do I praise Jesus?”
The real question is:
“Do I still follow Him when He doesn’t match my expectations?”
Because real discipleship is revealed under pressure.

When obedience becomes uncomfortable.
When answers are delayed.
When the path doesn’t make sense.
That’s where true loyalty is tested.

“The crowd was present for the entrance…
but absent at the cross.”
Don’t miss that.
Because it’s easy to follow Jesus when He’s being celebrated.
But will you stay when He’s being rejected?

Will you stay when obedience costs you reputation?
Comfort?
Control?
Will you stay when following Him feels lonely?
Because the cross reveals what the crowd could not sustain.
And here’s the deeper reality:

Jesus did not come to fit into your life.
He came to take over it.

He will bless you—but He will also break pride.
He will heal you—but He will also correct you.
He will lift you—but He will also lead you through surrender.

“Christ is not just someone to be admired.
He is Lord to be obeyed.”
And if we are not careful…

we can create a version of Jesus
who never confronts us,
never stretches us,
never calls us higher.
But that version of Jesus does not exist in Scripture.
The real Jesus will always lead you through transformation.
And transformation requires surrender.
So before you say “Hosanna” again…
ask yourself:

Is He only my Savior?
Or is He truly my Lord?

Because the most dangerous place to be
is not far from Jesus…

It is close to Him—
without ever surrendering to Him.

“The distance between praise and betrayal
is shorter than we think
when surrender is missing.”
May we not be people who celebrate Him in moments…
but resist Him in decisions.
May our worship go deeper than emotion.
May our faith survive discomfort.
May our loyalty remain—even when the crowd changes.
Because real love does not just wave palm branches.
It stays faithful… even at the cross.

Engagement Question:
Be honest—have you ever experienced a moment where following Jesus became uncomfortable, and you felt the tension between surrender and resistance?
